relations.subject: manage:server-group
relations.evidence: Server _groups_ can be administrator-defined to contain a number of the nodes within a Couchbase Cluster, and thereby protect the cluster against large-scale infrastructure failure.

notable_absence.finding: This page never names a required RBAC role for any server-group operation (create, delete, move-server, assign-group) - a genuine gap, since every other procedural page in this batch (create/edit/delete/flush a bucket) states its required role(s) explicitly in a Prerequisites section or inline sentence. A candidate relation (manage:server-group requiresServerRole role:full-administrator) was considered and DROPPED rather than asserted: the only textual support found elsewhere in the corpus (roles.md's generic statement that the Full Admin role exists) never states that it specifically gates server-group management, so asserting it here would have been reconstruction, not extraction.
notable_absence.finding_2: THE ROUND BRIEF'S NAMED HYPOTHESIS FOR THIS PAGE DID NOT HOLD. The dispatch briefing flagged this page as possibly overlapping with batch B's manage-users-and-roles.md ('RBAC groups'), but manage-groups/manage-groups.md is entirely about SERVER groups - administrator-defined groupings of cluster NODES for rack/availability-zone-style infrastructure-failure protection (Server Group Awareness) - and never once mentions RBAC groups, user groups, or role assignment. There is no overlap with manage-users-and-roles.md at all; the word 'group' names two completely unrelated Couchbase Server constructs (a node-placement construct here, a named set of users elsewhere), which is itself worth recording as a same-word-different-thing collision alongside the registry's existing four-way 'role' writeup. server:user-group (already promoted, the RBAC construct) and manage:server-group (this page's construct) share no relationship whatsoever.
